thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 502/504 spike detected for service/gateway in us-west-2. 5m error rate 6.8%. Detect link: https://redwood.example/alerts/3550009876 :rotating_light:

maria: I'm the oncall, looking now. Can someone confirm if any deploys happened in the last hour?

ajay: No deploys in last 60m from CI. I see a surge of downstream timeouts hitting origin-pool1, backend latency increasing to 850ms median.

samir: Traces are unusually sparse for these requests. Lots of entries missing request_id/span info. Could be sampler misconfig or an env var flip.

priya: If traces are sparse, we need stopgap instrumentation. Can we enable request-id propagation capture at the edge and add a temporary debug log flag? Suggest enabling an envoy header capture filter and bumping logging.

maria: Good call. We need quick steps: (1) add request_id to access logs, (2) enable debug for edge for 10m, (3) add short-lived metric for upstream_5xx_by_pool.

ajay: Pasting quick commands to toggle configmap and increase sampling:
```bash
# enable debug logging in gateway-config
kubectl -n prod patch configmap gateway-config -p '{"data":{"LOG_LEVEL":"debug"}}'
# bump tracing sampler (X-Ray/OpenTelemetry env var example)
kubectl -n prod set env deployment/gateway --containers=gateway TRACING_SAMPLER=1.0
```

observability-bot: Note: increasing sampling to 100% for 15m will increase ingestion ~10-15x. Confirm before proceeding. :eyes:

samir: Starting a 1% canary with the sidecar change to emit request_id in the logs now. Rolling svc-gateway-frontend debug sidecar -> 1% canary.

daniel: I'll push a small sidecar change that appends request_id to the access log. Rolling canary yamls now. If it looks good, will scale to 10%.

priya: Envoy snippet to capture header (for quick paste):
```yaml
- name: envoy.filters.http.lua
  typed_config:
    "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.lua.v3.Lua
    inline_code: |
      function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
        local rid = request_handle:headers():get("x-request-id") or "-"
        request_handle:logInfo("rid=" .. rid)
      end
```
Then apply as a patch to ingress.

ajay: Canary logs show request_id present now for the canary traffic. But overall 5xx still ~4.2% cluster-wide.

maria: Can we do a traffic shift away from pool1 to pool2 as a quick fallback? If pool1 is saturated or has a degraded backend, shifting might buy us time.

priya: Yes. Quick traffic-split change:
```bash
kubectl -n prod patch traffic-split gateway --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/backends/0/weight","value":30},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/backends/1/weight","value":70}]'
```
This moves 70% to pool2. We'll do incremental steps (30 -> 50 -> 70) over 5m.

maria: Customer impact (quick triage): Redwood-hosted customers see ~2% request failure in last 15m. Top affected: partner-acme (1.2% error), internal ingestion pipelines delayed. CS looped in.

daniel: Also prepared a short script to temporarily bypass prefix cache on small requests (to reduce backend latencies) — will run if shifting doesn't drop error rate.

ajay: After canary to 10% and initial weight shift (30/70), error rate dropped to 1.1%. Traces contain request_ids now and backfill is kicking in. Still watching latency.

maria: Pager handoff: I'm handing to @samir for the next 30 minutes while I brief CS and prepare the incident doc. @ajay please stay on standby for rollback or routing tweaks. :thumbsup:

samir: Taking pager. I'll keep monitoring and finalize mitigation notes. Adding timeline to incident doc: https://redwood.example/incidents/3550009876 :spiral_note_pad:

incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Traffic successfully shifted to pool2, 5xx rates returned to baseline. Follow-ups: 1) add invariant tests for request-id propagation, 2) add temporary increased trace sampling window for post-deploy 1h, 3) author postmortem and instrumentation runbook. Assigning to infra and observability teams. :white_check_mark:
